_comment: The trial registry: the product question each trial answers, and which EXISTING checker
answers each part of it. docs/trials.md is the policy; this is its executable form;
tools/trial.py is the only reader. `make trial T=<id>` runs one.
WHAT THIS FILE ALONE OWNS (nothing else in the repository states these):
question, criterion_version, scope, the required children and controls of each mode,
the property each child answers, the interpreter that reads the child's own evidence,
preservation, resource_class, timeout_s, and `requires` (assets whose absence is
NO VERDICT before anything runs).
WHAT IT ONLY REFERENCES (the referent is the source of truth; never copy it here):
dag_nodes -> docs/dag.json node ids. The receipt hashes each node's `covers` files
as the trial's dependency fingerprint; the file list lives in dag.json.
checker   -> a repo path. Its CLI, exit convention and evidence record are the
checker's own; `args` is only this trial's CHOICE of configuration
(which scenario, which preset), not a copy of the checker's inputs.
stage     -> retained evidence already committed, with the record that holds
its sha256. Staging refuses a file whose hash differs.
environment -> spec/trial-environment.json (the one dependency/tool spec that the
build box and CI both install from, via tools/trial_env.py).
RESULTS ARE NOT STORED HERE. A verdict exists only in a receipt under build/trials/,
generated by a run and checked by `tools/trial.py check-receipt`. There is no
`state` field to maintain by hand, and `~PASS` is not a value anything can take.
Placeholders in args: {out} = this child's fresh output directory, {root} = the
checkout. The checker runs as `<python> <checker> <args>`, cwd = the checkout.

T-RELEASE-BOUND.question: Do the selected Arty baseline image, its sources, the host CLI bytes, the supported domain and the evidence runs agree with one committed release manifest?

required.property: the committed release manifest equals a fresh derivation and every selected artifact agrees with every other
the Arty wrapper's bound digital proof covers every compiled source of this tree

check._controls_pending: No control yet, so this mode is NO VERDICT even when both children print BOUND (tools/trial.py composite; docs/trials.md rule 2). The control it needs is a STALE counterexample -- a manifest or binding fixture that release_manifest.py prints STALE for with exit 1 (interpret bound_text catches exactly that). release_manifest.py arrives with #255 and check_arty_evidence_binding.py takes no input path, so no such control can be written on this tree.

T-DEADLINE.question: Does the published Arty configuration meet the 256-cycle frame deadline at its pins, with complete I2S evidence equal to the model?
T-DEADLINE.criterion_version: deadline/1 (rtl-sketch/verify_deadline.py analysis v2: sample strobe <= 254, not busy at 255, zero missed frames, every required I2S period present once and equal to the model)

scope.domain: the Arty wrapper driven at its UART pins (scenario arty-uart); drum page at its reset image
excluded: the SPI full-kit stress scenarios (docs/deadline/README.md section 3)

sim.description: simulate the CURRENT tree's RTL in the Arty configuration

required.property: zero missed frames and I2S identical to the model over every required period

controls.intended_reason: a completion 160 cycles late is rejected as a DEADLINE miss, not an I2S mismatch

reanalyse.description: re-judge the RETAINED capture of the published image's sources (docs/deadline/traces, simulated at 2221d2c) under the current analysis; no simulation

required.property: zero missed frames and I2S identical to the model over every required period

controls.intended_reason: the retained late-completion capture is still rejected for the DEADLINE reason

T-PLAY-DIGITAL.question: Do the documented playback commands (the one-command held note per release preset, and a musical phrase through the rolling scheduler) produce correct, audible audio through the production control path UART -> RTL -> I2S?
T-PLAY-DIGITAL.criterion_version: play-digital/1 (held note: replay bit-exact AND decoded I2S peak >= 1024 LSB; phrase: every write executes on its frame and the wire I2S equals the model)

scope.path: uart_host CLI bytes -> arty_a7_top UART pins (RTL) -> decoded I2S

required.property: uart_host.py run --note 45 --fixture none is bit-exact at the pins and audible
uart_host.py run --preset m5a-saw --note 72 is bit-exact at the pins and audible
uart_host.py run --preset m5a-pulse --note 72 is bit-exact at the pins and audible
uart_host.py run --fixture demo: every write on its frame, and the RTL wire I2S equals the model over the whole phrase

controls.intended_reason: the pre-fix image (no mixer writes) replays bit-exact but is SILENT, and the level floor rejects it

T-LIVE-MIDI.question: Does a live MIDI stream, through the real host session and its bytes, drive the instrument with the documented note, drum and controller behaviour, explicit refusals, bounded queues, no stuck note, and receipt-to-update latency p95 <= 20 ms / p99 <= 30 ms under the declared load?
T-LIVE-MIDI.criterion_version: live-midi/1 (fpga/live_midi_contract.py: target, endpoints and declared load frozen before measurement; timing contract 2)

scope.path: deterministic MIDI -> fpga/midi_session.py -> UART bytes -> device contract (sim) and arty_a7_top UART pins (rtl) -> decoded I2S
excluded: hardware MIDI-to-audio latency (a later capture measurement)

sim.description: the session against the device contract on simulated time: coverage, counter wrap, pressure, the declared load; seconds

required.property: every scenario equals the independently built schedule on eleven properties and the declared load meets the latency target

controls.intended_reason: a lost note-off is caught by voice_gate and stuck_notes
GM 38 struck as the clap is caught by drum_strikes
one event 5 ms late is caught by timing

rtl.description: adds the session's own bytes replayed through the Arty UART wrapper, I2S compared with the model on the expected schedule, and two I2S controls

required.property: as sim, and the RTL wire I2S equals the model on the expected schedule for coverage, pressure and 3 s of the declared load

controls.intended_reason: a lost note-off is caught by voice_gate and stuck_notes
GM 38 struck as the clap is caught by drum_strikes
one event 5 ms late is caught by timing
